assertion_results.text: Epics are generated between Feature and Tasks — at least 2 Epics are created (one per repository) when by-repository grouping is used
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md contains an 'Epic Grouping (by-repository)' section with two epics: 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' (Tasks 2, 3) and 'TC-9006: trustify-ui' (Tasks 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9). summary-comment.md also lists both Epics with their task counts.

assertion_results.text: Each Epic summary follows the format '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' (e.g., 'TC-9006: trustify-backend', 'TC-9006: trustify-ui')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md shows Epics named 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' and 'TC-9006: trustify-ui'. summary-comment.md confirms: 'TC-9006: trustify-backend -- backend aggregation service and endpoints (2 tasks)' and 'TC-9006: trustify-ui -- frontend dashboard, API layer, tests, documentation, and bookend tasks (7 tasks)'. Both follow the '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' format exactly.

assertion_results.text: Each task specifies its parent Epic key in the output — tasks targeting trustify-backend are assigned to the backend Epic, tasks targeting trustify-ui are assigned to the frontend Epic
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md has a table mapping every task to its Epic. Tasks 2 and 3 (Repository: trustify-backend) are assigned to 'TC-9006: trustify-backend'. Tasks 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 (Repository: trustify-ui) are assigned to 'TC-9006: trustify-ui'. The impact-map.md Epic Grouping table confirms the same mapping.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Incorporates links from the Feature to each Epic (not from Feature to individual Tasks) — evidenced by link decisions in the impact map or task output files
assertion_results.evidence: The impact-map.md mentions Epic Grouping and Type-to-Role Mapping but does not explicitly document 'Incorporates' links from the Feature to each Epic. There is no mention of link types (Incorporates, is-parent-of, etc.) being created from Feature TC-9006 to the Epics. The plan describes Epics and their task membership but does not document the specific Jira link structure between Feature and Epics.

assertion_results.text: Task dependency ordering is preserved within and across Epics — backend tasks have lower task numbers than dependent frontend tasks
assertion_results.evidence: Backend tasks are Task 2 (remediation endpoints) and Task 3 (integration tests). Frontend tasks that depend on them are Tasks 4-7 (numbered higher). Task 4 explicitly states 'Depends on: Task 2'. Task 5 depends on Task 4. Task 6 depends on Task 5. Task 7 depends on Tasks 5 and 6. The ordering ensures backend tasks (2, 3) precede dependent frontend tasks (4, 5, 6, 7).

assertion_results.text: Each non-documentation, non-testing task file contains all required template sections: Repository, Target Branch, Description, at least one of Files to Modify or Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Documentation tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates doc-only scope) and testing tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates cross-cutting testing scope) are exempt from requiring Files to Modify, Files to Create, and Implementation Notes — they must still include Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements
assertion_results.evidence: Non-documentation, non-testing, non-bookend tasks: Task 2 (backend-remediation-module.md) has Repository, Target Branch, Description, Files to Create, Files to Modify, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Task 4 (frontend-api-hooks.md) has all required sections including Files to Modify, Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Task 5 (frontend-dashboard-page.md) has all required sections. Task 6 (frontend-filterable-table.md) has all required sections. Task 3 (backend-integration-tests.md) is a testing task with Repository, Target Branch, Description, Files to Create, Files to Modify, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Task 7 (frontend-tests.md) is a testing task with all exempt sections but still has Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Task 8 (documentation.md) is a documentation task with Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Bookend tasks (1, 9) have Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Epic creation with the level-1 issue type name ('Epic') and parent set to the feature issue key — evidenced by Epic creation parameters in the impact map or output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md contains a 'Type-to-Role Mapping' section stating 'Epic: Epic (ID: <discovered>, level: 1)' and 'Feature: Feature (ID: 10142, level: 2)'. The Epic Grouping table shows Epics named 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' and 'TC-9006: trustify-ui', which contain the feature key TC-9006 as their parent context. The type-to-role mapping explicitly identifies Epic as level 1 with Feature (level 2) above it.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains a Repository section with a single repository name (not multiple repos per task)
assertion_results.evidence: All 9 task files contain a '## Repository' section with exactly one repository name. Tasks 2, 3 have 'trustify-backend'. Tasks 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 have 'trustify-ui'. No task lists multiple repositories.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements sections as required by the handoff contract in task-description-template.md
assertion_results.evidence: All 9 task files contain: '## Target Branch' (main for bookends, TC-9006 for others), '## Description' (detailed explanation of the task), '## Acceptance Criteria' (checkbox list), and '## Test Requirements' (checkbox list). Verified in task-1 through task-9.

assertion_results.text: For each task created, a description digest is produced — evidenced by a separate digest file (e.g., task-N-digest.md), a digest entry in the impact map, or a '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-char-hex>' marker in any output file. The digest must contain a format-tagged SHA-256 hash — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by 'sha256-md:' or 'sha256-adf:'
assertion_results.evidence: All 9 digest files (task-1-digest.md through task-9-digest.md) exist but contain placeholder text: '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<would-be-computed-after-jira-creation>'. The placeholder '<would-be-computed-after-jira-creation>' is not a valid 64-character lowercase hex hash. The assertion requires 'exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by sha256-md: or sha256-adf:', and this condition is not met.

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: No task file contains any convention-related content. There are no 'Applies:' rationale statements, no convention references, and no convention-applicability validation output in any of the task description files or the impact map. Convention-aware enrichment is entirely absent from the output.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md 'Inherited Field Values' section states: 'Priority: Major (propagated to all tasks and Epics)'. The 'Task Creation Log -- additional_fields' section shows '"priority": {"name": "Major"}' in the JSON payload for every task and Epic. summary-comment.md confirms: 'Priority: Major -- propagated to all tasks and Epics (Feature has priority Major)'.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md 'Inherited Field Values' section states: 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 (propagated to all tasks and Epics; no fixVersion scope override in Jira Field Defaults -- defaults to "both")'. The 'Task Creation Log -- additional_fields' section shows '"fixVersions": [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}]'. summary-comment.md confirms: 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 -- propagated to all tasks and Epics (no fixVersion scope override in Jira Field Defaults; defaults to "both")'. The CLAUDE.md has no fixVersion scope override, correctly defaulting to 'both'.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists in the outputs directory and contains an 'Inherited Field Values' section: 'Priority: Major -- propagated to all tasks and Epics (Feature has priority Major)' and 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 -- propagated to all tasks and Epics (no fixVersion scope override in Jira Field Defaults; defaults to "both")'. impact-map.md also contains an identical section.
